sections.title: Maintenance Request Form
sections.context: A tenant is calling the apartment maintenance office to report several issues in her flat.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Good morning. Oakwood Manor Maintenance Office, Alex speaking. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Oh, hello. I'm calling because I've got a few things in my apartment that need fixing. I moved in just last month, and a couple of issues have started cropping up.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear that. I'll get a work order started for you. First, could I have your full name, please?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Yes, it's Sarah Jenkins.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Thank you, Ms. Jenkins. And which apartment are you in?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: I'm in 42B... oh, wait, I'm so sorry, that was my old unit number in the previous building. I'm actually in 51C now. It's on the fifth floor.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: No problem at all. 51C, Oakwood Manor. And do you have a contact number where our technician can reach you if they have trouble finding the place?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Yes, my work number is 07700 900 123, but I'm rarely at my desk. You'd better take my mobile. It's 07700 900 546.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Let me just double-check that... 07700 900 546. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: That's the one. Now, about the repairs. The most urgent thing is in the kitchen. There is a leaking tap under the sink. It's not just a drip; there's actually a small puddle forming every few hours.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: A leaking tap, right. That sounds like it might need a new washer or perhaps a whole new fixture. I'll mark that as a priority. Is there anything else?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Yes, in the master bedroom, the window latch is broken. I can't seem to lock it properly, which makes me feel a bit uneasy at night, even though I'm on the fifth floor.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: I understand. Security is important. I'll make a note of the bedroom window. Any other maintenance concerns?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Actually, yes. One of the lights is acting up. The one in the hallway is flickering constantly. It’s quite distracting when I’m moving between rooms.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Hallway light flickering. Got it. It might be a loose connection or just an old bulb. We'll have a look. Now, we need to schedule a time for Mark, our technician, to come over. Would tomorrow morning work for you?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: I'm afraid I have a meeting all morning tomorrow. Is Wednesday available?

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Let me see... Wednesday morning is quite busy. He has an opening at 9:30, but that might be too early? Or he could come by at 11:15.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: 11:15 would be perfect. I should be back from my errands by then.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Great. Now, in case you are delayed, will you be leaving a key for him, or should he come back another time?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: If I'm not there, I will leave a key with the concierge at the main entrance. He knows me well.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: That's very helpful. Just a few more details for the technician. Do you have any pets in the apartment that he should be aware of?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: I do have a cat. She’s very friendly, but she might try to sneak out if the door is left open for too long. I'll try to keep her in the living room while he works.

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: Good to know. And finally, I have to inform you that since you've been here less than a year, these repairs are covered, but for future reference, there is usually a service charge of fifteen pounds for non-emergency visits after the first twelve months.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Oh, I see. A service charge. That's good to know for the future. Hopefully, I won't have too many more problems!

transcript.speaker: Alex
transcript.text: We hope so too. We'll see you on Wednesday at 11:15, Ms. Jenkins. Have a nice day.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Thank you, goodbye.
